To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the magnetic hyperthermia efficiency of core-shell nanoparticles depends on the damping ratio of surface to core spins, the exchange parameter of the interface and the anisotropy of the surface and core.

the magnetic hyperthermia performance of core-shell nanoparticles can be improved by reducing the surface to core ratio of the damping factor and by increasing the exchange coupling between the core and the shell.

core-shell nanoparticles with a high surface to core damping ratio, a large interface exchange parameter and a surface anisotropy lower than the core one are the most efficient ones in magnetic hyperthermia.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of magnetic hyperthermia in core-shell nanoparticles.
the development of an analytical model for the magnetic hyperthermia phenomenon in core-shell nanoparticles.

the development of a theoretical model for the magnetic hyperthermia phenomenon of core-shell nanoparticles, which is an emerging and promising therapy for the treatment of many diseases, mainly for the treatment of cancer.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the magnetic hyperthermia efficiency of core-shell nanoparticles depends on their size, composition, surface to core damping ratio and the interface exchange parameter.

the most efficient magnetic hyperthermia is obtained by selecting materials and tuning parameters to minimize the ratio of the surface to core spin damping factors, increase the interface exchange coupling and tune the surface to core magnetocrystalline anisotropy ratios for each material combination.
the most efficient magnetic nanoparticle for cancer treatment is the one with the lowest surface anisotropy and highest surface exchange coupling.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the heat generation efficiency of nanoparticles can be increased by reducing the ratio of the surface to core magnetic damping, increasing the interface coupling and tuning the anisotropy of the surface and core.
the most efficient hyperthermia nanoparticles should have the following properties: (i) high magnetization, (ii) high surface to core damping ratio and (iii) high interface exchange coupling.
the heat generation efficiency of nanoparticles depends on the material properties and the nanoparticle size, but the latter is not the most relevant parameter.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the surface spins are the most efficient ones for heat generation, and that the core-shell structure of nanoparticles can enhance their heat generation efficiency.
the surface to core spin damping factor ratio is a key quantity to be optimized in the design of magnetic nanoparticles for magnetic hyperthermia applications.
the heat dissipation of core-shell nanoparticles is not only determined by the core size but also by its surface properties.
